notes:
PDF has exactly 2 physical pages (confirmed via pdfinfo page-count metadata only; no content/text extraction tool was used). Page 1 = Semesters One-Six. Page 2 = Semesters Seven-Eight followed by the Graduation Requirements Summary numeric table, numbered footnotes 1-12, Program Notes, University Requirements, and the Codes legend (all correctly excluded from `sections` per instructions). No column-header row is repeated at the top of page 2 before "Semester Seven."

KEY TRAP (the reason this doc was selected): the Prerequisites column in this table is center-justified, not left-aligned. When a prerequisite sentence wraps, the overflow text is horizontally centered under the (wide) Prerequisites column, which sits roughly in the right half of the page. In at least two rows the *entire* second line consists of nothing but a bare, wrapped course number, sitting alone and visually far to the right of the row's course title:
  - Semester Three, "ECHE 310 Intro. to Chem. Engr. Thermodynamics (or ENCP 290)": prerequisite text is "C or better in ECHE 300; Prereq or Coreq: MATH 241" — "241" alone occupies the second line, centered.
  - Semester Five, "ECHE 440 Separation Process Design fall only": prerequisite text is "C or better in ECHE 300; Prereq or Coreq: ECHE 311" — "311" alone occupies the second line, centered.
I rendered the PDF myself at 300 DPI with pdftoppm (a pure rasterizer, not a text/content extractor) and visually zoomed into these exact rows to confirm the layout before transcribing; both prerequisite cells above are the single, unbroken strings shown, and neither "241" nor "311" is a credit-hours value — the true Credit Hours cell for both rows is "3", printed on the row's first line, far to the left. A parser doing column assignment by raw x/y text position (rather than proper row/cell reconstruction) could easily grab that isolated wrapped number and misfile it as a Credit Hours entry (a bare 1-3 digit token is exactly what a real credit-hours cell looks like). A third, superficially similar row — Semester Eight, "ECHE 466" — wraps as "...Prereq or Coreq: ECHE 322," / "567", but there the trailing "567" is NOT alone on its line (it shares the line with "ECHE 322,"), so it's a weaker/less clean instance of the same failure mode; I flag it for completeness only.

MISSING COLUMN (schema gap, not an omission on my part): the printed table has a "Program GPA" column (footnote 2) between "Min. Grade" and "Code," populated with a bare "*" for courses that count toward the major/program GPA (e.g., ECHE 101, ECHE 300, ECHE 310, ECHE 311, ECHE 320, ECHE 321, ECHE 322, ECHE 430, ECHE 440, ECHE 456, ECHE 460, ECHE 461, ECHE 465, ECHE 466, ECHE 550, ECHE 567, the "Engineering Elective" rows in Semesters Six and Eight, and "Professional Development Elective" in Semester Three) and blank otherwise. The given row schema has no field for this column, so its value is not represented anywhere in `rows` — this is intentional on my part, not a data-entry gap, and a parser/grader should not expect this column's asterisks to surface elsewhere.

Stacked/two-line Code-column values are joined with "/" (matching the instructions' own example "MR/CC-INT," which is in fact this exact document's ECHE 466 row): ENGL 102 -> "CC-CMW/CC-INF"; ECHE 466 -> "MR/CC-INT"; PHIL 325 -> "CC-CMS/CC-VSR". All other multi-line wraps (titles, prerequisites) were joined with a single space per the general instruction.

Course-title footnote digits are fused verbatim exactly as printed (e.g., "Calculus 13" = "Calculus 1" + footnote superscript 3; "Chemistry Lab Electives6," "Carolina Core GHS7," "Carolina Core GFL12," etc.) with no reinterpretation.

Two title-text inconsistencies are preserved verbatim as printed rather than "fixed": "PHYS 211L Essentials of Physics I Lab" (no trailing period) vs. "PHYS 212L Essentials of Physics II Lab." (trailing period present) — this asymmetry is in the source PDF, not a transcription error.

"!" (critical) markers, Min. Grade letters, and blank cells were all individually re-verified against 300-DPI zoomed crops of every row, not just the initial full-page read, specifically to catch any row where a "!" or letter grade might have been misattributed to an adjacent row during line-wrapping.
